clue.text: Keep original dialect

indicators.note: original is read in its sense of novel or newly made, so the letters of dialect are made into something new

explanation.surface: A linguist praises the authentic local speech of a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: the strong central tower of a castle. 'original' is the anagram signal working on 'dialect'.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified stronghold at the heart of a castle, the same thing as a fortress.

clue.text: College head keen to meet demand

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so take the first of College

parts.note: to be all for something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: A college principal eager to satisfy a call from the students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College head' looks like the principal, but 'head' takes only its first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: To call for something is to require or insist on it.

clue.text: Loftier kind of ornamentation

indicators.note: kind of signals a sort or variety of the word, here a rearranged version of loftier

explanation.surface: A more elevated style of decoration is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: A trefoil is a three-lobed decorative motif used in Gothic tracery, a piece of architectural ornament.

clue.text: Agreed about Rex being idler

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for agreed goes round the letter for king

parts.note: done! is said to accept a deal, so it means agreed
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Everyone accepts that the king is a lazy layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male bee that does no work, so the word is used for a lazy person, a loafer.

clue.text: Measure pine item due to be replaced

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
it is the pronoun standing for a thing, an item

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so the letters of due are rearranged

explanation.surface: A due pine is being swapped out for a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be replaced' rearranges DUE into UDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Longitude is a measurement, in degrees, of a position east or west of Greenwich.

clue.text: Second one rushed over to bring cocktail

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for rushed is written backwards

parts.note: rushed means raced

explanation.surface: A second drinker hurried across to fetch a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RACED into DECAR. 'to bring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Nail spray

definitions.meaning: a small headless tack, as used in glazing
a small shoot or twig of a plant, as in a spray of heather

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a small headless tack, and a little shoot of a plant used as decoration.

clue.text: Tread path warily: it's dangerous

indicators.note: to move warily is to pick an uncertain course, so the letters of tread and path are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning to step carefully along a hazardous track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warily' rearranges TREAD and PATH together.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathtrap is a place or vehicle so unsafe it could kill, a perilous thing.

clue.text: Laugh at the northern apprentice IN THE SPIRIT OF RUGBY stuck in routine job

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Laugh at the northern apprentice IN THE SPIRIT OF RUGBY stuck in routine job', has OCR headline text inserted; CHORE around T and L needs a word for T that the held words do not clearly give, and no reprint was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Laugh at the northern apprentice IN THE SPIRIT OF RUGBY stuck in routine job

clue.text: Thief gives sigh, starting to rob

parts.note: the wind sighs or rustles in the leaves, both soft breathy sounds

indicators.note: starting to takes the first letter of the word that follows, rob

explanation.surface: A robber lets out a sigh as he begins a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is a cattle or horse thief.

clue.text: Rest weren't honest, admit it

parts.note: to have told untruths is to have lied
to own up is to admit, so own means admit

explanation.surface: A guilty party is told to confess they were not truthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to take a rest, recline for a nap.

clue.text: Argues for common sense, up to a point

parts.note: reason is sound judgment, common sense
S is south, one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone makes the case for good sense, but only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a point' is a compass point, S. 'for' and 'up to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to argue logically or present a case.

clue.text: Blooming fellow's looking gloomy

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a lowering sky is dark and threatening, looking gloomy

explanation.surface: A man looks thoroughly fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British expletive describing the fellow; it is the definition, in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant is in bloom.

clue.text: Do loathe taking out a pension

indicators.note: do is used in the sense of arrange or fix up, so the letters of loathe are rearranged

parts.note: a is the letter removed from the letters

explanation.surface: Someone really detests withdrawing a retirement payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking out' removes the A from LOATHE before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension in France and elsewhere is a boarding house or small hotel.

clue.text: Regulation number laid down

parts.note: a rule is a regulation
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a number

explanation.surface: A rule decides how many items are put down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid down has been decreed, settled by authority.

clue.text: Fancy man?

parts.note: a fancy man is slang for a lover, but read as a man one fancies it describes a very attractive man

explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is an attractive man someone has a crush on.

clue.text: Foreign articles found beside brook — teddies, etc?

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
der is the German definite article
to brook something is to bear or wear it, as in not wearing any nonsense

explanation.surface: Imported clothing turns up beside a stream, including soft toys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teddies' are not toys here but a one-piece women's undergarment. 'found beside' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddies are lingerie, an example of clothes worn next to the skin.

clue.text: Bent police officer stood out by the way

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
shone means excelled or stood out
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A corrupt cop was conspicuous on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for corrupt or crooked.

clue.text: Sees lace's knotted without end?

indicators.note: knotted means tangled together, so the letters of sees and lace's are twisted

parts.note: the s here counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone notices lace in knots that seem endless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knotted' rearranges SEES and LACES; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceaseless means never stopping, without a pause.

clue.text: King bestowing honour on Rhone town

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award
Arles is a town on the Rhone in Provence

explanation.surface: A monarch confers a title on a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bestowing' and 'on' are links; in a down clue CH sits on top of ARLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles is the name of several British kings.

clue.text: American, a learner coming in to fillet seafood delicacy

indicators.note: coming in to means entering, so the letters go inside the word for fillet

parts.note: to fillet a fish is to bone it
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A US novice chef helps prepare a gourmet shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: A and L go inside BONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is a large edible sea snail prized as a luxury food.

clue.text: Nut and mushroom turnover, a new starter

indicators.note: a turnover is something turned over, so the word for mushroom is written backwards

parts.note: a cep is a porcini mushroom

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so take the first letter of new

explanation.surface: A menu offers a nut-and-mushroom pastry and a fresh appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like a pastry, but it turns CEP into PEC. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecan is a nut from a hickory tree.

clue.text: No longer attached to work

definitions.meaning: detached, as a button or handle that has fallen away
succeed, as a plan that works out

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to become detached and to be successful.

clue.text: It may be home to Clare

definitions.text: It may be home to Clare

parts.words: It may be home to Clare
parts.note: Clare looks like a woman's name, but it is a member of the Poor Clares, an order of nuns

explanation.definitionFit: A convent of nuns is where a Poor Clare, a Franciscan nun, would live.

clue.text: Panic like troops at the rear

indicators.note: at the rear says the troops come after the word for like

parts.note: a la means in the manner of, like
RM is the Royal Marines, troops

explanation.surface: Fear spreads like wildfire among soldiers at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a sudden fear, a fright.

clue.text: Outdoor type, maybe, son tramps on

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible version, so the letters of son and tramps are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lad hikes onwards, perhaps a lover of the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges SON and TRAMPS; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman is someone who hunts, shoots or fishes, a lover of field sports.

clue.text: One put in to satisfy French composer

indicators.note: put in to means placed inside, so the letter goes into the word for satisfy

parts.note: to sate is to satisfy fully
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A single item is added to please a composer from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer of the early 20th century, known for his Gymnopedies.

clue.text: Narrow recorder

definitions.meaning: to grow thinner towards one end
one who records, as on tape

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to thin to a point, and someone who tapes things.

clue.text: Careful to discover future prospects

definitions.meaning: the call to beware, take care
outlook, as in a bleak outlook for the economy

explanation.walkthrough: 'to discover' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a warning to be careful; the noun means one's prospects or outlook.

clue.text: Consider late opening is out of line

parts.note: ex means former, late

indicators.note: is out of puts the opening outside, round the letter for line

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a tardy start is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: PORE goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore an idea is to examine or look into it.

clue.text: Female officer, one with English sheepdog

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
LT is short for lieutenant
the Roman numeral for one is I
E is for English

explanation.surface: A woman police officer works with a single English collie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltie is a Shetland sheepdog.

clue.text: Saving plant at the end of the day

parts.note: thrift is a coastal plant, the sea pink

indicators.note: at the end of the takes the last letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Gardening economically: a plant bought at the close of trading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of the day' reads as a cliche meaning 'in the end'; here it takes the last letter of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrifty means economical, careful with money.
